history.summary: Prominent Durga shrine in Varanasi built in the 18th century by Rani Bhabani (Bhavani) of Natore, Bengal, in North Indian Nagara style with a red-ochre exterior and multi-tiered shikhara representing the five elements (panchmahabhutas). The main idol is believed to be swayambhu (self-manifested, not crafted), and the Skanda Purana tradition holds that Durga guards Kashi from the south. The temple was renovated by Maratha rulers in the 19th century. It stands beside the rectangular Durga Kund tank; shrines of Lakshmi, Saraswati, Kali, Hanuman and Bhairavnath are in the complex. Each Nag Panchami the kund reenacts Vishnu reclining on the serpent. NOTE: opening-hour conflict across sources (5 AM–12 PM / 4–9 PM vs 4 AM–1 PM / 3–8 PM — verify).

name: Durga Temple
town_description: Varanasi (Banaras/Kashi) is one of the world's oldest living cities, on the banks of the Ganga in Uttar Pradesh. India's spiritual capital, it is famed for the Kashi Vishwanath Temple, its ghats, Banaras Hindu University, and silk weaving.

travel.airport: Lal Bahadur Shastri International Airport, Varanasi, ~25-26 km
travel.road: On Durgakund Road near Tulsi Manas Temple and Banaras Hindu University, ~2 km south of the old city

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Navratri (September-October) for peak festivities
visitor_information.opening_hours: 5:00 AM–12:00 PM and 4:00 PM–9:00 PM daily; some sources list 4 AM–1 PM and 3–8 PM — verify. Entry free.
